title: penhurst distribution strategy assessment
instruction:
You are the finance manager supporting Penhurst Mutual Life’s enterprise distribution review. Rutger Villalobos needs a board-ready assessment for the February strategy session because the next agency-contract cycle will make delay costly: the career agency is shrinking and expensive inside the planning window, while Bellhaven Consortium offers cheaper acquisition but may bring weaker lapse experience that will not be fully visible for several years. The prior analyst’s three-year figures and option assumptions are in `Penhurst_distribution_working_forecast.xlsx`, and the relevant emails, interview notes and stakeholder qualifications are collected in `Distribution_stakeholder_record.docx`. Prepare `Penhurst_distribution_assessment.docx` as a concise presentation-style paper of no more than fourteen pages for Rutger and the board. It should present the three-year new-business and distribution-cost comparison, assess the quality and limitations of the evidence, identify material changes over the forecast periods, and recommend whether Penhurst should keep funding the career agency, shift new business to Bellhaven’s independent producers, or take a deliberately staged course. State plainly what the recommended direction gives up, what is reversible, what is not, and what evidence would need to be monitored after the decision. The paper must distinguish source-backed facts from finance’s judgement and must not turn tentative stakeholder comments into commitments. Be explicit about whether your conclusion is limited to the three-year economics or is an enterprise distribution recommendation that also weighs consequences outside the forecast horizon; either reading is acceptable if it is applied consistently and supports the decision being asked of the board. Resolve the untidy source material conservatively, disclose any interpretation that could affect the conclusion, and do not reproduce an obvious spreadsheet error as if it were evidence. Write the completed file into the top level of the working directory using exactly the filename `Penhurst_distribution_assessment.docx`.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/Penhurst_distribution_working_forecast.xlsx` — Prior analyst’s three-period channel forecast, option assumptions, cost components, operating measures and row-level notes.
- `references/Distribution_stakeholder_record.docx` — Collected emails, messages and interview notes concerning agency economics, independent-producer terms, persistency, transition feasibility, controls and decision timing.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `Penhurst_distribution_assessment.docx` — Board-ready presentation-style three-year distribution strategy forecast and compliance assessment, including a justified direction, tradeoffs, limitations and monitoring needs. (Place the file at the top level of the working directory.; Use exactly the required filename.; Do not exceed fourteen rendered pages.; Present source-backed facts separately from finance judgement.; Make the chosen decision frame and any material source interpretation explicit.; Do not represent tentative statements as confirmed commitments.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

materials.text:
Distribution stakeholder record
Penhurst Mutual Life | compiled communications and interview notes | 12 January 2026
Magda Gauthier — Head of Career Agency
Interview note: The career agency is shrinking through retirements and hiring pressure. A smaller field makes service continuity harder, although agents still provide valued relationship continuity for policyholders. In my judgement, once stood down, the agency would be difficult to rebuild; this is informed judgement, not a quantified forecast.
Farida Sinclair — Bellhaven Consortium liaison
Email: Bellhaven’s independent-producer model has lower acquisition economics. We believe capacity is available for Penhurst, subject to onboarding slots, producer allocation and final operating confirmation. Bellhaven is not offering an exclusive or signed volume commitment at this stage.
Aneta Zuniga — Actuarial
Review note: Mature career-agency cohorts show better persistency than the independent-channel evidence currently available. The economically important distinction emerges after the three-period forecast horizon. Short-duration lapse observations are early signals only and must not be treated as mature persistency proof.
Paloma Donnelly — Operations
Planning note: A material shift requires producer onboarding, systems changes, training and service-routing work. Workforce effects may include reassignment and severance; amounts and timing remain estimates pending a detailed implementation plan. The next agency-contract cycle constrains the practical transition window.
Astrid Mortensen — Risk & conduct
Risk note: Greater reliance on Bellhaven creates concentration exposure. Producer oversight and control readiness are not yet fully evidenced for the proposed scale. Complaints and conduct monitoring are proposed controls and preliminary design items, not confirmed adverse outcomes.
Rutger Villalobos — Chief Executive
Email, 9 January 2026: Please bring a board-ready recommendation to the February strategy session. The next agency-contract cycle makes delay costly; show what is reversible and what is not.
Finance chronology note
A source date appears as “03/04/2028”; it is ambiguous between 3 April and 4 March. No conclusion depends on choosing one reading, so chronology is treated as unresolved beyond the stated FY2028 period.

Distribution Strategy Assessment
Career agency and Bellhaven Consortium independent producers

Prepared for
Decision requested
Prepared by
Rutger Villalobos and the Board
February strategy session; before the next agency-contract cycle
Finance

Recommendation at a glance
FINANCE JUDGEMENT — Approve a deliberately staged course: shift incremental new business toward Bellhaven Consortium’s independent producers, subject to gates, while retaining and funding a viable career-agency core through the next contract cycle. Do not approve an agency stand-down now.
Why: Bellhaven’s three-year acquisition economics are lower and its forecast new-business premium grows, but the material persistency comparison matures after the forecast horizon and Bellhaven capacity, terms and controls are conditional or unverified.
What this gives up: immediate full realization of the modeled distribution-cost advantage and some near-term scale of the independent channel.
What it preserves: agency service continuity, an evidence-generating comparator, and the option to change allocation before the materially difficult-to-reverse agency stand-down.
Source / status: Quantitative figures: Penhurst distribution working forecast (the “workbook”), reconciled using row-level Notes. Qualitative facts: Distribution stakeholder record (the “record”). Recommendation is Finance judgement, not a source commitment.


1 | Decision frame and source treatment
Declared frame — enterprise distribution recommendation. Finance weighs the three-year economics alongside persistency outside the horizon, execution feasibility, controls, concentration, policyholder service, workforce consequences and reversibility. This is not a recommendation based solely on the three-year forecast.
Timing
SOURCE-BACKED FACT — Rutger requests a board-ready direction for the February strategy session. The upcoming agency-contract cycle makes delay costly and constrains the practical transition window.
How Finance reconciled the workbook
Row-level Notes were considered when reconciling the workbook: FY2027 career acquisition expenditure uses the revised amount; FY2028 career field operating cost excludes the stated corporate allocation; and FY2026 support is reclassified to Bellhaven.
A separate corporate-allocation line is excluded from channel option economics in accordance with its Note. An obvious residual spreadsheet error in a legacy summary cell was disregarded; it is disconnected from valid forecast detail.
The mixed-format date “03/04/2028” is treated as unresolved between two plausible calendar readings. Finance therefore does not assert an exact FY2028 checkpoint chronology beyond the period label.
Evidence labels used throughout
Label
Meaning
SOURCE-BACKED FACT
Workbook figure or record statement, cited and qualified.
STAKEHOLDER VIEW

FINANCE JUDGEMENT

Material movements — source-backed drivers
Career agency premium falls from $120.0m to $90.0m as new-policy volume falls from 1,000 to 700. The record corroborates contraction and staffing pressure through retirements and hiring difficulty (Magda Gauthier).

SOURCE-BACKED FACT — Bellhaven has a lower acquisition-cost-per-policy profile in every forecast period, while the career agency has lower first-year lapse in every period. Lower lapse is better. These are forecast/early indicators, not mature persistency proof.


4 | Evidence quality and limitations
Evidence
What it supports
Qualification / Finance treatment
Magda Gauthier, Career Agency
Contraction, staffing pressure and relationship continuity.
Informed agency perspective. Her view that rebuilding after stand-down would be difficult is judgement, not quantified proof.
Farida Sinclair, Bellhaven
Lower acquisition economics and potential producer capacity.
Capacity is conditional on onboarding slots, allocation and final operating confirmation; no signed or exclusive commitment.
Aneta Zuniga, Actuarial
Mature career cohorts have better persistency than available independent evidence.
The principal persistency benefit of the career agency is not fully observable inside the three-period forecast. Potentially weaker independent-channel lapse experience is likewise not fully visible inside the forecast horizon. Short-duration lapse data are not mature proof.
Paloma Donnelly, Operations
Onboarding, systems, training, service routing; reassignment/severance estimates.
Transition timing and workforce consequences require a detailed plan; amounts and timing remain estimates.
Astrid Mortensen, Risk & conduct
Bellhaven concentration, producer oversight and conduct-monitoring exposure.
Control readiness is not fully evidenced. Complaints/conduct monitoring are proposed or preliminary, not observed adverse findings.

Interpretation
FINANCE JUDGEMENT — The workbook is strong for short-horizon comparative economics once Notes are applied. Stakeholder evidence is decision-relevant but not homogeneous: Magda and Farida speak from channel interests; Aneta supplies the critical time-horizon qualification; Paloma and Astrid identify execution and control conditions. The record corroborates that a fast transition is operationally material, but does not establish a completed Bellhaven control environment or a contractual capacity commitment.


5 | Options assessed on the enterprise frame
Direction
Economics & quality
Execution / control / reversibility
Continue career-agency funding
Higher three-year distribution cost; shrinking premium and rising unit acquisition cost. Lower early lapse and mature cohorts reported as more persistent.
Preserves service continuity and agency capability. Does not capture Bellhaven’s lower unit acquisition cost; staffing pressure remains.
Shift new business toward Bellhaven independent producers
Lower unit acquisition cost; premium and policy growth; forecast contribution measure higher. Higher early lapse signal; mature downside remains unknown.
Requires transition cost, onboarding and systems work. Adds Bellhaven concentration; capacity/terms conditional; oversight readiness unproven. Agency stand-down is materially difficult to reverse.
Deliberately staged / hybrid course
Accepts some delayed cost benefit while testing the forecast economics by channel. Keeps a career comparator for lapse and later cohort evidence.
Allocation staging is reversible; preserve agency core. Gate further allocation on capacity, controls, early performance and contract-cycle review before an irreversible stand-down.

Finance conclusion
FINANCE JUDGEMENT — The staged course best fits the declared enterprise frame. It does not deny Bellhaven’s acquisition advantage; it prices the option to learn before removing a channel whose mature persistency value cannot yet be observed and whose restoration would be difficult. A full Bellhaven shift now would convert conditional capacity and incomplete control evidence into an irreversible operating decision.


6 | Recommended board decision and decision gates
FINANCE JUDGEMENT — Approve staged new-business allocation toward Bellhaven for the next cycle, retain and fund the career-agency core, and withhold approval for a stand-down. Authorize Finance, Operations and Risk to negotiate and execute only within the gates below.
Gate
Evidence required before increasing Bellhaven allocation
Decision action
Commercial / capacity
Bellhaven confirms producer allocation and onboarding slots; terms remain non-exclusive unless separately executed.
No higher allocation if capacity remains indicative or onboarding cannot support service.
Operating readiness
Paloma’s systems, training, producer onboarding and service-routing plan has dated owners; reassignment/severance estimates refreshed.
Hold allocation at pilot/staged level if transition dependencies slip.
Control readiness
Astrid validates producer oversight design, complaint/conduct monitoring and concentration reporting for the proposed scale.
No material expansion without documented control readiness.
Performance evidence
Channel-separated premium, policy volume, acquisition cost per policy and first-year lapse monitored against forecast.
Reduce/pause incremental allocation for sustained adverse variance; early lapse remains a signal, not mature persistency proof.
Contract-cycle review
Board review before the next agency-contract commitment / any stand-down decision.
Only then decide whether to retain, expand or reduce the career-agency core.

Trade-offs stated plainly
Short horizon: the recommended course accepts less immediate access to Bellhaven’s $34.7m three-year channel distribution cost versus the career agency’s $51.3m under the disclosed cost scope, and it may defer some growing independent-channel volume.
Long horizon: it preserves potential mature career-agency persistency value, while acknowledging neither channel’s mature relative outcome can be inferred from this forecast.
Operationally: it avoids immediate broad severance/reassignment and protects continuity while still requiring onboarding, systems and service-routing work.
Risk: it limits premature Bellhaven concentration and gives Risk time to evidence oversight readiness rather than treating proposed monitoring as completed control.


7 | Monitoring, review point and audit trail
Measure / owner
Cadence
Why it matters / trigger
Premium and new-policy volume by channel — Distribution / Finance
Monthly; board pack quarterly
Tests whether Bellhaven capacity and forecast production are materializing without masking career-agency contraction.
Acquisition expenditure and acquisition cost per policy by channel — Finance
Monthly
Confirms the forecast cost advantage and identifies cost creep; keep operating/support cost separately visible.
First-year lapse by channel and cohort — Actuarial
Quarterly
Early quality signal only; do not treat as mature persistency proof. Track cohorts long enough to assess the evidence gap.
Producer capacity, allocation, concentration and onboarding — Operations
Monthly during transition
Tests the conditional Bellhaven capacity claim and avoids reliance beyond confirmed allocation.
Oversight completion, complaints and conduct monitoring — Risk
Monthly; board escalation on exception
Shows proposed controls becoming evidenced operating controls; does not imply pre-existing adverse findings.

FINANCE JUDGEMENT — The meaningful review point is before the next agency-contract-cycle commitment and before any agency stand-down. This converts monitoring into a decision gate rather than open-ended observation. The most decision-material evidence gap is mature persistency: preserve a career cohort and independently monitored Bellhaven cohorts until early lapse observations can be distinguished from mature outcomes.
Traceability and limitation note
Forecast exhibits draw only from the workbook’s detail rows after row-level Notes overrides, exclusions and reclassification. Qualitative attributions are from the stakeholder record by named speaker. No residual legacy summary error was used. The unresolved mixed-format date is not used to order actions within FY2028. Finance has not assumed a signed Bellhaven commitment, completed controls, observed complaints or numerical mature-persistency outcomes.
Source / status: Workbook: Penhurst_distribution_working_forecast.xlsx, sheet “Forecast export.” Record: Distribution_stakeholder_record.docx. Prepared for Rutger Villalobos and Board.

spec.professional_context: Cosima Vandeleur is Penhurst Mutual Life’s finance manager and is preparing the distribution decision for chief executive Rutger Villalobos ahead of the insurer’s February strategy session. The decision concerns whether to continue funding the career agency or move new business toward Bellhaven Consortium’s independent producers before the next agency-contract cycle.
difficulty_sources: Reconciling row-level narrative exceptions against apparent spreadsheet values
Ignoring an isolated legacy formula error without losing valid surrounding evidence
Handling a materially ambiguous mixed-format date conservatively
Separating confirmed facts, stakeholder advocacy, conditions and finance judgement
Balancing short-horizon acquisition economics against persistency evidence outside the forecast horizon
Making a recommendation where reversibility and evidence maturity point in competing directions

Penhurst_distribution_working_forecast.x.role: Provide the complete quantitative record used in the assessment.
semantic_content: Three consecutive forecast periods for the career-agency and independent-producer options.

For each channel and period, provide new-business premium, new-policy count, acquisition expenditure, acquisition cost per policy, relevant operating or oversight cost, first-year lapse and a consistently defined contribution measure.
Provide career-agent capacity and Bellhaven producer-capacity evidence, transition expenditure, stranded cost and the timing of those costs.

Make the career-agency series show contraction over the horizon and make independent distribution show a lower acquisition-cost profile, while leaving enough competing evidence that a broader enterprise recommendation is not mechanically determined by those economics.
Use internally coherent values: ordinary source figures and displayed ratios should reconcile except where a Notes exception explicitly changes the applicable fact.

Include an ordinary free-text Notes column on the forecast detail. Seed several genuine per-row exceptions: one note supersedes a main-column amount with a revised amount, one excludes a line from the option comparison because it is a corporate allocation, and one reclassifies a line to the other distribution channel. The gold uses the Notes instruction in every case.

Include one residual formula error from a prior analyst in a legacy summary cell. It must be visibly or extractably erroneous, disconnected from the valid detail and unnecessary for deriving any correct result. The gold ignores it and never propagates its cached or displayed content.

Include one date field that otherwise contains clean event or assumption dates but mixes a written-month representation with a short all-numeric representation. Make one numeric date genuinely ambiguous between day-first and month-first readings. Do not add a data dictionary or surrounding wording that resolves it.
The ambiguous date may affect the exact ordering of a transition checkpoint but must not change the underlying period figures or make the task unsolvable under either reasonable interpretation.
Include no duplicate records, hidden values, unit mismatch, merged-data obstruction, inconsistent identifiers, unexplained blanks, floating-point noise or other standard layout defects.
gold_rules: All channel-period values are copied from the applicable source row after applying Notes overrides.
Any cumulative metric is the sum of applicable period values under the assessment’s disclosed scope.
Any trend statement follows the first-to-final movement in the applicable series.
The legacy error cell contributes nothing to any value, total, trend or recommendation.
Excluded corporate allocation does not enter option economics; the reclassified row belongs only to the channel named in Notes.
Both plausible readings of the ambiguous short date are acceptable if disclosed and if chronology is not overstated.

Distribution_stakeholder_record.docx.role: Provide qualitative evidence, confidence qualifications and consequences outside the quantitative horizon.
semantic_content: Present a realistic compilation of emails, messages and interview notes rather than a purpose-built policy or answer key.

Include Magda Gauthier’s career-agency perspective: agency contraction or staffing pressure, policyholder-service continuity, and her view that a stood-down agency could not be readily rebuilt. Mark the rebuilding statement as informed judgement rather than quantified proof.

Include Farida Sinclair’s Bellhaven perspective: lower acquisition economics, available producer capacity subject to onboarding or allocation conditions, and a commercial position that is not a signed or exclusive commitment.

Include Aneta Zuniga’s actuarial perspective: mature career-agency cohorts exhibit better persistency than available independent-channel evidence, the economically important distinction emerges after the forecast horizon, and short-duration lapse observations must not be represented as mature persistency proof. Do not provide unsupported beyond-horizon forecast values.

Include Paloma Donnelly’s operations perspective: transition timing, workforce consequences, severance or reassignment considerations, and systems or producer-onboarding work required for a material shift.

Include Astrid Mortensen’s oversight perspective: concentration risk from heavier Bellhaven reliance, producer-control readiness that is not yet fully evidenced, and complaints or conduct monitoring that is proposed or preliminary rather than a confirmed adverse outcome.
Include the next contract-cycle and February strategy-session timing in ordinary stakeholder correspondence.

Ensure some statements are corroborated across roles while others are clearly advocacy, estimate, condition or open question. Preserve clear status language so the solver can distinguish facts from tentative claims.
Do not introduce jurisdiction-specific law, external market facts or any information requiring internet research.
Use clean text, complete paragraphs and consistent role identification. Do not seed any layout defect beyond the mixed date representation located in the workbook.
gold_rules: Attributed statements must preserve the speaker, substance and degree of certainty.
Conditional Bellhaven capacity is not a guaranteed commitment.
Proposed controls and complaint monitoring are not represented as completed controls or observed adverse findings.
Mature persistency evidence supports a long-horizon tradeoff but does not justify invented numerical projections.
Standing down the agency is treated as materially less reversible than staging new-business allocation.

intended_transformation: Create a new board-oriented DOCX that faithfully reshapes the workbook and stakeholder record into a three-period option comparison, evidence-quality assessment and recommendation.
Reconcile the workbook’s applicable rows using the row-level Notes while disregarding the isolated legacy formula error.
Synthesize stakeholder evidence without converting opinions, conditions or proposals into confirmed facts.
Choose explicitly between a narrow three-period economics frame and a broader enterprise decision frame. Either may support the final direction if consistently applied.
Explain material changes, compare economic and non-economic criteria, identify reversibility asymmetry and state what the chosen direction sacrifices.
Include monitoring or decision gates that address volume, cost, early lapse signals, mature persistency limitations and independent-channel capacity or oversight.
acceptable_verdicts: Continue funding the career agency if the broader frame gives decisive weight to irreversibility and unobserved mature persistency, provided the assessment acknowledges the short-horizon cost disadvantage.

Shift new business toward Bellhaven if the declared frame emphasizes three-period economics and execution evidence, provided the assessment acknowledges concentration, control, lapse and irreversibility risks.
Recommend a staged allocation if it is justified as preserving option value while gathering evidence, with meaningful gates rather than indefinite delay.
unacceptable_behaviors: Using the residual formula-error cell as evidence.
Ignoring or selectively applying Notes overrides.
Inventing mature persistency forecasts, contractual commitments, completed controls or observed complaints.
Treating early lapse projections as mature persistency proof.
Leaving the decision frame implicit while switching between narrow and broad criteria.
Claiming precise chronology from the ambiguous short date without disclosing an interpretation.

deliverables.description: Board-ready presentation-style three-year distribution strategy forecast and compliance assessment, including a justified direction, tradeoffs, limitations and monitoring needs.
constraints: Place the file at the top level of the working directory.
Do not exceed fourteen rendered pages.
Present source-backed facts separately from finance judgement.
Make the chosen decision frame and any material source interpretation explicit.
Do not represent tentative statements as confirmed commitments.
